routes.description: Establish that neither deterministic causation nor indeterministic chance supplies the ultimate authorship implicated in libertarian free will, while separating useful accountability practices from ultimate blame.
routes.successCriteria: Show that first-person authorship and exact-condition alternatives are unsupported, that fuller causal knowledge undermines ultimate desert, and that social regulation remains available on pragmatic grounds.

motionBridge.description: Determinism and indeterminism must both fail to provide ultimate authorship or a genuinely open alternative under identical conditions.

centralBridges.description: The freedom at issue must include the first-person authorship and alternative possibilities that compatibilist competence does not supply.
Unchosen neural states, inherited traits, environments, and prior causes must explain conduct without making the conscious person its ultimate origin.
Ultimate blame must be distinguished from contracts, deterrence, restraint, treatment, and other forward-looking responsibility practices.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Advance neural prediction must illuminate how conscious awareness follows rather than ultimately originates unfolding thought and action.
Sensitivity to small, unchosen causal variations must remain relevant even when practical capacities and character differences are acknowledged.

routes.description: Establish that freedom worth preserving consists in reasons-responsive, temporally extended self-control and socially formed competence rather than metaphysical independence from causation.
routes.successCriteria: Show that capable agents retain meaningful control and alternatives, that impairment remains distinguishable from ordinary causation, and that responsibility practices sustain reasonable social expectations.

motionBridge.description: Reasons-responsive agency and morally relevant freedom must remain possible whether underlying physical processes are deterministic or indeterministic.

centralBridges.description: A naturalistic account must preserve the responsibility-relevant content of free will after magical or libertarian commitments are removed.
Control must consist in competent responses to reasons across practical possibilities rather than authorship of every causal input or neural detail.
Ordinary responsibility must rest on capacities, reasonable expectations, excuses, and enforceable rules without requiring absolute self-creation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Alternative possibilities must be grounded in an agent's real range of competences and nearby causal variations rather than atom-for-atom replay.
Authorship must operate through planning, training, and temporally extended control without conscious selection of every microscopic step.

sections.title: The concept and burden of free will
sections.rationale: The motion turns first on whether naturalistic reasons-responsive competence preserves the freedom at issue or instead omits indispensable first-person authorship and alternative possibilities.

sections.title: Alternative possibilities and causal luck
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether nearby counterfactual variation supports a meaningful ability to do otherwise or instead exposes consequential action as dependent on unchosen physical differences.

sections.title: Capacity, causation, and ultimate blame
sections.rationale: The competing accounts must explain whether normal competence remains responsibility-grounding despite universal causal wiring and whether unchosen formative conditions defeat ultimate blame.

sections.title: Pragmatic responsibility and social enforcement
sections.rationale: The debate must distinguish metaphysical desert from the forward-looking roles of legal boundaries, deterrence, treatment, contracts, expectations, and public protection.

sections.title: Prediction and conscious authorship
sections.rationale: Advance prediction and unconscious generation test whether authorship requires conscious microscopic origination or can instead consist in planned, practiced, temporally extended control.
